embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: At native scale, the raised palm connects through its forearm and sleeve to the same woman; the lower supporting hand connects to her opposite arm. There are no transferred working hands.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: The raised arm bends forward from a relaxed shoulder and elbow to the cloth; the lower arm reaches a nearby waist-level tab. Both reach distances are ordinary and connected.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: The torso and apron descend coherently toward the off-frame floor, with both hands carrying only the light curtain. No visible load-bearing or balance contradiction is present.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: The upper palm and fingertips lie on the linen face with a coherent boundary; the lower fingers curl around the curtain/tab edge with room behind the cloth. Both contacts are assessable.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: The face, both connected working hands, curtain grid and small tab coexist in the same saved frame. The rail and curtain extend beyond the top/right crop, but the critical hand-to-cloth and hand-to-tab relations remain visible.

supplemental_artistic_review.first_impression_without_control_labels: An intimate workshop portrait of a person checking a small repair. The face and broad yellow textile lead, with a quiet touch and tiny red tab making a specific completed task readable.
supplemental_artistic_review.subject_presence: Face, short dark bob, gentle mouth and unforced shoulder/arm posture feel coherent with the working setting.
supplemental_artistic_review.hierarchy: The face is the first hook; the raised hand leads to the grid and the lower hand leads to the red repair tab.
supplemental_artistic_review.causal_scene: Scissors and clipped red thread on the bench support a repair just finished; the still does not prove future return to use or a real occupation.
